findings.quote: urging them to save themselves, and warning that destruction was not far off if they did not take better counsel for themselves.
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna (***) after παρακαλῶν σῴζειν σφᾶς αὐτούς; the following clause εἶναι δὲ τοῦτον οὐ μακράν has no surviving antecedent for τοῦτον. The English smooths this by supplying 'destruction'.
findings.proposed_fix: urging them to save themselves [gap in the Greek] and saying that this was not far off if they did not take better counsel for themselves.

units.note: Thyrreium/Thyrium spelling not flagged (not an identity error). Chapter end is mid-word (τη-) continued by ch.30 (-ροῦντες); the English handles the join acceptably.

Numbers checked: 200 talents, 300 in six years at 50 a year, six months, 150 talents, 180 stades all match. The Greek itself says Lucius Cornelius here but Lucius Quinctius in ch.32; English follows each faithfully.

findings.quote: In particular Leon son of Hicesias seemed to have spoken well in other respects
findings.problem: Greek: καὶ γὰρ ἐδόκει μετὰ Δάμων᾽ ὁ Κιχησίου λέων ἄλλα τε καλῶς εἰπεῖν. 'For' (καὶ γάρ, explaining why the senate relented) and the words μετὰ Δάμωνα (after Damon) are dropped; the patronymic Κιχησίου is Cichesias, not Hicesias.
findings.proposed_fix: For Leon son of Cichesias, speaking after Damon, seemed to have spoken well in other respects

units.note: The text is printed with the odd elision Δάμων᾽; Damon is presumably the Rhodian spokesman. Rest of chapter checked and accurate.

findings.quote: The people of the Aetolians shall maintain the rule and supremacy of the Roman people in good faith.
findings.problem: Greek: τὴν ἀρχὴν καὶ τὴν δυναστείαν τοῦ δήμου τῶν Ῥωμαίων * **. The sentence breaks off in a lacuna; the verb and 'in good faith' are not in the Greek, they are invented to smooth the gap.
findings.proposed_fix: The people of the Aetolians shall ... the rule and supremacy of the Roman people [gap in the Greek].

findings.quote: And whenever the Romans are at war with anyone, the people of the Aetolians shall also be at war with them.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) immediately before καὶ ἐὰν πολεμῶσιν πρός τινας Ῥωμαῖοι; the English reads on as if the text were continuous and the clause were a plain continuation of the preceding clause.
findings.proposed_fix: [gap in the Greek] ... and if the Romans are at war with anyone, the people of the Aetolians shall be at war with them.

units.note: Numbers checked (100 days, 200 talents, 1 mina gold per 10 silver, 50 talents x 6 years, 40 hostages, ages 12-40, six years) all match. Lucius Quinctius and Gnaeus Domitius correct. English 'these are to be handed over within one hundred days' is somewhat ambiguous as to antecedent (Greek ἐν ἡμέραις ἑκατὸν governs the whole ἀποδότωσαν clause); not flagged.
Fragment; identity of Fulvius and the citadel not determinable from the excerpt.

findings.quote: he took measures to prevent any importation of funds gathered from outside.
findings.problem: Greek: περιεβα... γένοιτο κομιδὴ τῶν ἔξω ποριζομένων χρημάτων. The word περιεβα... is truncated/corrupt, but there is no negative (no μή); γένοιτο κομιδή means there should be a bringing-in of funds procured from abroad. The English inverts the sense ('prevent') and hides the break.
findings.proposed_fix: he [the Greek breaks off here] ... so that there might be a supply of funds procured from outside.

units.note: Greek corrupt at περιεβα...; the main verb cannot be restored, so no verb is proposed.
Two unrelated fragments; both rendered accurately.
